John Locke on experience

John Locke (1632–1704) approaches experience within Empiricism. Ideas originate in experience; legitimate political authority rests on consent and protects life, liberty, and property. Systematically, the teaching links experience, rights, government into a practical and theoretical whole. On this page, the archive isolates English passages where that project meets experience most directly—useful for searches such as “john locke quotes on experience.”

How to use this page

Start with the shortest passage, then compare tone across sources. Return to the John Locke thinker page for biography and to the experience theme for other voices on the same question.
